proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true lag is closer to 2 weeks or varies over time, forecasts may show systematic lead/lag around the peak and during rapid rise/decline.
proposals.rationale: Prioritize robustness with a minimal latent-to-observed lag: SEIR is parsimonious for a single-season, moderately peaky series, and a 1-week delay captures plausible admission/reporting lag without relying on precise phase alignment.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May over-smooth timing if admissions respond faster than 2 weeks in some periods, producing delayed peak timing and underestimating early growth.
proposals.rationale: Same low-variance SEIR core with a 2-week delay, matching the previously best-performing delay while avoiding the higher-variance 3-week alignment; intended as a stable baseline for hospitalization-rate-as-lagged-infection-proxy semantics.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: With only 31 training points, the extra degree of freedom can absorb noise, leading to unstable inferred seasonality/turning points and reduced rolling robustness.
proposals.rationale: Adds waning immunity as a controlled complexity increase while keeping the observation mapping simple and the delay short; included only as a check for improved rolling stability versus SEIR in this age group.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Identifiability issues between waning immunity and transmission can cause drift in mid-season levels and degrade multi-week-ahead forecasts despite good in-sample tracking.
proposals.rationale: Carries forward the prior best template but constrains delay to the more stable {1,2} set; tests whether SEIRS provides consistent rolling-only gains over SEIR when the lag is set to 2 weeks.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H-state parameters may be weakly identifiable in a short series, causing unstable hospitalization scaling/duration and sensitivity to initialization, which can hurt rolling-only performance.
proposals.rationale: Single explicit hospitalization-state alternative consistent with target semantics; kept to one SEIHR variant to limit overfitting while allowing a mechanistic admission process rather than a pure lagged-I proxy.
